children: said Monday it plans to invest $420 million to expand its manufacturing operations in Camden, Arkansas, adding 650 full-time jobs over five years.
The expansion will increase production capacity for several missile systems, including Patriot Advanced Capability-3, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense interceptors and Precision Strike Missiles.
For investors, the investment signals continued demand for missile defense systems as Lockheed
expands manufacturing capacity to fulfill military contracts. Lockheed shares have gained 32% this year, compared with an 11% advance for the S&P 500 Index (

The announcement follows Lockheed's January groundbreaking for a Munitions Acceleration Center in Camden, part of an agreement with the Pentagon to increase annual THAAD interceptor production from 96 to 400 units.The new facility will incorporate robotics, digital manufacturing technologies and workforce training to support production of THAAD, PAC-3 and other weapons systems.

Lockheed's Camden operations currently employ approximately 1,100 workers across a 2.2-million-square-foot manufacturing complex. The site produces seven major U.S. military weapons programs, including HIMARS rocket launchers and ATACMS missiles.

Camden site general manager Adam Bailey said the expansion would accelerate weapons production and strengthen the company's manufacturing capabilities. Lockheed didn't provide a completion date for the project.

title: Lockheed Martin to invest $420M in Arkansas missile production expansion
